Alternatively, for every quantum state at the senders end, there exist d-encoding operations which produce d-orthogonal quantum states. Transmitting which via a d-level perfect quantum channel it is possible to communicate log d-bits of classical information. But what if the set of encoding operations is restricted only within a physically constrained class? Here, we consider such a class of encoding operations to be the set of free operations for any quantum resource theory and show that the constrained capacity - namely, the free encoding capacity (FEC) emerged as a unit of the corresponding quantum resource. Moreover, we show that for the pointed resource theories - a resource theory admitting only a single free state - FEC becomes a faithful resource measure also. We also discuss the implications of FEC in the question of resource-theoretic state transformations and the possibility of extending its faithfulness for general quantum resource theories.

AI.tldr: The paper introduces Free Encoding Capacity (FEC) as a unit of quantum resources, showing it emerges from constrained encoding operations in quantum resource theories and becomes a faithful resource measure for pointed resource theories.
AI.motivation: The motivation is to understand how classical information capacity changes when encoding operations are restricted to physically constrained classes (free operations in quantum resource theories), and to establish a connection between information-theoretic capacity and resource quantification.
AI.method: The authors consider encoding operations restricted to free operations of any quantum resource theory, define Free Encoding Capacity (FEC) as the constrained capacity under these restrictions, and analyze its properties for general and pointed resource theories.
AI.result: FEC emerges as a unit of the corresponding quantum resource, and for pointed resource theories (those admitting only a single free state), FEC becomes a faithful resource measure. The paper also explores implications for resource-theoretic state transformations and potential extensions to general quantum resource theories.
AI.conclusion: The Free Encoding Capacity provides a fundamental connection between information transmission capacity and quantum resource quantification, serving as both a capacity measure under constrained encoding and a faithful resource measure for pointed resource theories, with broader implications for resource theory foundations.

title: Compact U(1) Lattice Gauge Theory in Superconducting Circuits with Infinite-Dimensional Local Hilbert Spaces
summary: We propose a superconducting-circuit architecture that realizes a compact U(1) lattice gauge theory using the intrinsic infinite-dimensional Hilbert space of phase and charge variables. The gauge and matter fields are encoded directly in the degrees of freedom of the rotor variables associated with the circuit nodes, and Gauss's law emerges exactly from the conservation of local charge, without auxiliary stabilizers, penalty terms, or Hilbert-space truncation. A minimal gauge-matter coupling arises microscopically from Josephson nonlinearities, whereas the magnetic plaquette interaction is generated perturbatively via virtual matter excitations. Numerical diagonalization confirms the emergence of compact electrodynamics and coherent vortex excitations, underscoring the need for large local Hilbert spaces in the continuum regime. The required circuit parameters are within the current experimental capabilities. Our results establish superconducting circuits as a scalable, continuous-variable platform for analog quantum simulation of non-perturbative gauge dynamics.

AI.tldr: Superconducting circuit architecture realizes compact U(1) lattice gauge theory using infinite-dimensional rotor Hilbert spaces, with gauge and matter fields encoded directly in circuit nodes, exact Gauss's law from local charge conservation, and all interactions emerging naturally from circuit physics.
AI.motivation: To develop a scalable, continuous-variable platform for analog quantum simulation of non-perturbative gauge dynamics using superconducting circuits, overcoming limitations of auxiliary stabilizers, penalty terms, and Hilbert-space truncation in existing approaches.
AI.method: Encode gauge and matter fields directly in rotor variables (phase and charge) of superconducting circuit nodes. Gauss's law emerges exactly from local charge conservation. Gauge-matter coupling arises from Josephson nonlinearities, magnetic plaquette interaction generated perturbatively via virtual matter excitations. Numerical diagonalization validates approach.
AI.result: Numerical diagonalization confirms emergence of compact electrodynamics and coherent vortex excitations, demonstrating need for large local Hilbert spaces in continuum regime. Required circuit parameters are within current experimental capabilities.
AI.conclusion: Superconducting circuits establish a scalable, continuous-variable platform for analog quantum simulation of non-perturbative gauge dynamics, with exact gauge symmetry and natural emergence of gauge-matter interactions from circuit physics.

title: Complete Hierarchies for the Geometric Measure of Entanglement
summary: In quantum physics, multiparticle systems are described by quantum states acting on tensor products of Hilbert spaces. This product structure leads to the distinction between product states and entangled states; moreover, one can quantify entanglement by considering the distance of a quantum state to the set of product states. The underlying optimization problem occurs frequently in physics and beyond, for instance in the computation of the injective tensor norm in multilinear algebra. Here, we introduce a method to determine the maximal overlap of a pure multiparticle quantum state with product states based on considering several copies of the pure state. This leads to three types of hierarchical approximations to the problem, all of which we prove to converge to the actual value. Besides allowing for the computation of the geometric measure of entanglement, our results can be used to tackle optimizations over stochastic local transformations, to find entanglement witnesses for weakly entangled bipartite states, and to design strong separability tests for mixed multiparticle states. Finally, our approach sheds light on the complexity of separability tests.

AI.tldr: A method using multiple copies of pure quantum states to compute maximal overlap with product states, providing hierarchical approximations for entanglement quantification with applications to separability tests and complexity analysis.
AI.motivation: The need to quantify entanglement through distance to product states, which is a fundamental optimization problem in quantum physics with applications in tensor norm computation, separability testing, and understanding computational complexity.
AI.method: Introduces a method based on considering several copies of a pure multiparticle quantum state to determine maximal overlap with product states, leading to three types of hierarchical approximations that provably converge to the actual value.
AI.result: The hierarchical approximations converge to the actual maximal overlap value, enabling computation of geometric measure of entanglement, optimization over stochastic local transformations, finding entanglement witnesses for weakly entangled states, and designing strong separability tests for mixed states.
AI.conclusion: The approach provides a systematic method for entanglement quantification with guaranteed convergence, offers practical applications in quantum information processing, and provides insights into the computational complexity of separability tests.

title: High-gain effects in broadband continuous-wave parametric down conversion sources and measurements with undetected photons
summary: We study theoretically how high-gain effects affect the measurement outcome of visible signal spectra in undetected photon measurement schemes. We consider two interferometric configurations: firstly, the SU(1,1) interferometer where the idler incurs loss and additional dispersion in between two identical, lossless, squeezers; secondly, the induced coherence interferometer where the idler incurs loss and additional dispersion in between two identical, lossless, squeezers and where the second squeezer is seeded by the idler and a vacuum ancilla mode. Furthermore, we consider a distributed loss configuration where the idler incurs loss as it propagates in the nonlinear medium. Motivated by experimental evidence and due to the fact that broadband sources are ideal for these measurement schemes, we use the dispersive data of a third-order dispersion engineered integrated waveguide parametric down conversion (PDC) source presented in New Journal of Physics 26, 123025 (2024) to model the PDC spectra in the three configurations. For each configuration we consider the case of idler-only (i) absorption, (ii) additional dispersion, and (iii) the combined effects. We obtain results which outline the strength and weaknesses of the different configurations at different operation points.

AI.tldr: Analysis of how high-gain effects impact visible signal spectra measurements in undetected photon schemes using three interferometric configurations with idler loss and dispersion.
AI.motivation: To understand how high-gain effects influence measurement outcomes in undetected photon measurement schemes, particularly examining the impact of idler loss and dispersion on visible signal spectra across different interferometric configurations.
AI.method: Theoretical study of three configurations: 1) SU(1,1) interferometer with idler loss/dispersion between two identical lossless squeezers, 2) induced coherence interferometer with similar setup but seeded by idler and vacuum ancilla, 3) distributed loss configuration where idler incurs loss during propagation in nonlinear medium. Uses dispersive data from a third-order dispersion engineered integrated waveguide PDC source to model spectra.
AI.result: Obtained results outlining strengths and weaknesses of different configurations at various operation points, analyzing cases of idler-only absorption, additional dispersion, and combined effects.
AI.conclusion: The study provides comparative analysis of how different interferometric configurations perform under high-gain conditions with idler loss and dispersion, identifying operational advantages and limitations for each setup in undetected photon measurement schemes.

title: Understanding multiscale disorder in superconducting nanowire single photon detectors
summary: Superconducting nanowire single-photon detectors are central to applications across quantum information science. Yet, their performance is limited by the effects of disorder and electrodynamic inhomogeneities that are not well understood. By combining DC transport, dark-count measurements, and bias-dependent microwave transmission spectroscopy in the presence of controlled nanoscale disorder introduced through helium-ion irradiation, we distinguish local instability-driven processes from intrinsic superconducting depairing and kinetic inductance nonlinearities. This approach enables systematic tuning of kinetic inductance, depairing currents, microwave dissipation, and mode structure within a single device. Bias- and temperature-dependent resonance shifts quantify disorder-induced modifications of the superconducting density of states through the nonlinear kinetic inductance, while the emergence of multiple resonant modes reveals the formation of electrodynamically distinct superconducting regions. Comparing depairing under current, field, and temperature isolates the dominant microwave loss mechanisms, separating vortex, quasiparticle, and two-level-system contributions, thus providing a robust multifunctional foundation for disorder engineering of superconducting nanowire detectors and resonators.

AI.tldr: Combined transport, dark-count, and microwave spectroscopy on helium-ion irradiated superconducting nanowires reveals disorder effects on kinetic inductance, depairing currents, and microwave dissipation, enabling systematic disorder engineering for improved detector performance.
AI.motivation: Superconducting nanowire single-photon detectors are limited by disorder and electrodynamic inhomogeneities that are not well understood, hindering their performance in quantum information applications.
AI.method: Combined DC transport, dark-count measurements, and bias-dependent microwave transmission spectroscopy on superconducting nanowires with controlled nanoscale disorder introduced through helium-ion irradiation.
AI.result: The approach enables systematic tuning of kinetic inductance, depairing currents, microwave dissipation, and mode structure; bias- and temperature-dependent resonance shifts quantify disorder-induced modifications of superconducting density of states; multiple resonant modes reveal formation of electrodynamically distinct superconducting regions; comparison of depairing mechanisms isolates dominant microwave loss contributions (vortex, quasiparticle, two-level-system).
AI.conclusion: The methodology provides a robust multifunctional foundation for disorder engineering of superconducting nanowire detectors and resonators by distinguishing local instability-driven processes from intrinsic superconducting properties and enabling systematic control of device parameters.

title: Robust multiparameter estimation using quantum scrambling
summary: We propose and analyze a versatile and efficient multiparameter quantum sensing protocol, which simultaneously estimates many non-commuting and time-dependent signals that are coherently or incoherently coupled to sensing particles. Even in the presence of control imperfections and readout errors, our approach can detect exponentially many parameters in the system size while maintaining the optimal scaling of sensitivity. To accomplish this, scrambling dynamics are leveraged to map distinct signals to unique patterns of bitstring measurements, which distinguishes a large number of signals without significant sensitivity loss. Based on this principle, we develop a computationally efficient protocol utilizing random global Clifford unitaries and evaluate its performance both analytically and numerically. Our protocol naturally extends to scrambling dynamics generated by random local Clifford circuits, local random unitary circuits (RUCs), and ergodic Hamiltonian evolution--commonly realized in near-term quantum hardware--and opens the door to applications ranging from precise noise benchmarking of quantum dynamics to learning time-dependent Hamiltonians.

AI.tldr: A quantum sensing protocol that simultaneously estimates many non-commuting, time-dependent signals using scrambling dynamics to map signals to unique measurement patterns, achieving exponential parameter scaling with optimal sensitivity.
AI.motivation: To develop a versatile quantum sensing protocol that can simultaneously estimate multiple non-commuting and time-dependent signals in practical settings with control imperfections and readout errors, overcoming limitations of existing approaches.
AI.method: Leverages scrambling dynamics to map distinct signals to unique patterns of bitstring measurements. Uses random global Clifford unitaries for efficient implementation, with extensions to local Clifford circuits, random unitary circuits, and ergodic Hamiltonian evolution.
AI.result: The protocol can detect exponentially many parameters in system size while maintaining optimal sensitivity scaling. It remains robust to control imperfections and readout errors, and is computationally efficient.
AI.conclusion: The protocol enables simultaneous estimation of many non-commuting signals with practical quantum hardware, opening applications in noise benchmarking and learning time-dependent Hamiltonians.
